title: Summer trips to Europe as a soloist
summary: Edison took summer leaves to tour Copenhagen, Holland and Switzerland, and mentions the Glen Campbell show and band integration.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Then -- but I did so many shows around here. In the meantime, I still recorded with Frank Sinatra. I always recorded with him. And then I would go to Europe like as a soloist, you know, before Jaws and I got together, as a soloist.
Well, you played with rhythm sections over there.
Yes. Go to Copenhagen and stay there for about two, about three weeks. Then I'd go to Holland and a couple of nights and to Switzerland. You know, I'd just stay

over there for about three or four weeks and then I'd come back. It wasn't an extensive tour like I do now with Jaws. But Copenhagen is fantastic place to go. You know, they got some good musicians there. I'd come back and resume my studio work, you know.
You could always pick it up.
I always left -- I'd get a leave of absence, you know, and -- because during the summer months, the show would terminate, you know, and --
-- for the summer, that's when I'd take off.
And I did the Glen Campbell show when he substituted for the Smothers Brothers. That was his start --
How integrated are those bands now for shows like that?
Well, it depends on the contractor.
